page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the average tier for compute and memory tasks. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations. In stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both single-core and multi-core performance fall within the middle 50% of tested servers. However, memory performance shows some bottlenecks; while cached small-block reads reach 465.3 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads of 37.76 GB/sec and the overall Passmark memory score are positioned in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and physics simulations show weaker relative performance.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.ce4.2xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or heavy parallel GPU computing. It is well-suited for applications such as caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis (where it achieves 8.03 million SET operations per second), static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications. It is less suitable for large-scale LLM inference or heavy database operations that depend on high-speed uncached memory access.
